findings.title: Reject terminal results that do not match the stored receipt
findings.body: When a terminal task receives a same-status result with a different canonical payload/hash, this branch treats it as a harmless duplicate without comparing the incoming result to the stored `worker_task_results.result_sha256`. The OMP adapter therefore returns the old hash and the TypeScript bridge reports the new transport as accepted even though its summary/result was never durably recorded, allowing an alternate result to be falsely acknowledged; compare the incoming receipt hash with the stored one and reject mismatches.

findings.title: Authenticate the parent marker before propagating ancestry
findings.body: A worker prompt can contain a user-controlled string matching `SECOND_BRAIN_WORKER_TASK`; `mirrorWorkerContextReceipt` takes the first match and stores its `parent_session_id` without checking that the task/packet belongs to this dispatch. With this new propagation, the next child mirror invokes `ledger init --parent-session` for that arbitrary valid host session, attaching the child ledger (and its budget contribution) to an unrelated root or failing initialization; derive ancestry from the pending dispatch/Brain task record rather than trusting prompt text.

findings.title: Reject usage records without a matching session identity
findings.body: The accounting loop only raises when `session` is present and different, so a malformed usage record with no `session` (or a null one) is still summed for the requested session. A truncated/hand-edited alias file can therefore add arbitrary tokens and force a false SOFT/HARD budget decision instead of the documented `ACCOUNTING_UNAVAILABLE` fail-open result; require an exact session identity before adding usage.

FinalCodeAudit.explanation: The candidate still trusts a task-text marker as the authoritative parent, so a crafted worker prompt can redirect ancestry and the hard-cap parent lookup before ledger initialization; it also treats missing-session telemetry as valid usage, allowing malformed records to drive a false budget state. The native framing, populated-governor latency, missing live qualification/deployment/economics, and baseline Pyright issues remain explicit HOLD gates rather than being treated as resolved.

findings.title: Deduplicate usage records across telemetry aliases
findings.body: `_session_telemetry_paths` returns both the raw and sanitized filenames, but `_session_total_tokens` adds every `assistant_usage`/`model_invocation_completed` record from both files without an event-level identity check. When both writers contain the same session usage (the exact dual-file case this repair supports), one provider turn is charged twice and can falsely reach SOFT/HARD, so merge aliases by a stable usage-event identity or select one canonical record before summing.

findings.title: Exercise index-level parent propagation before claiming root proof
findings.body: The closeout calls canonical root linkage an offline-proven capability, but the only `index.ts` regression sends a child marker without `parent_session_id`; it verifies the telemetry receipt yet never verifies `workerParentSessions` is populated or that a later mirror forwards `--parent-session`. The separate ledger-mirror unit test supplies the option directly, so an integration wiring regression could pass all cited tests while new workers still initialize rootless; add a marker-to-mirror assertion or narrow the claim to unit coverage and retain it as unverified integration.

FinalEvidenceAudit.explanation: The closeout is appropriately HOLD, but its offline-proof summary overstates canonical root-linkage coverage: the integration path that extracts a child marker and applies the parent to later mirrors is not exercised by the cited regression. The raw/sanitized telemetry files establish an alias path, but do not prove duplicated billing, because the records have no shared invocation identity.

corrections.reason: Reviewer could not identify a supported producer or stable shared invocation identity. Equal totals may be distinct charges; historical alias had usage in only one file.

Reviewer acknowledged identical OMP retries acquire a new created_at during normalization. Terminal same-task/packet/status replay deliberately returns the first authoritative receipt; no alternate content is persisted or forwarded. Receipt immutability remains unchanged.
Report14 and ancestry report narrow direct boundary proof versus native marker-to-ledger integration.
